title: Maritime Central Airways 315
summary: Maritime Central Airways Flight 315, a Douglas DC-4 on charter from London to Toronto with stops in Reykjavík and Goose Bay, crashed in bad weather near Issoudun, Quebec. While flying at approximately 6,000 feet near Quebec City, the aircraft flew into a cumulonimbus cloud, encountered severe turbulence, and lost control in a near-vertical dive.
probable_cause: The aircraft flew into a cumulonimbus cloud while enroute. Severe turbulence caused the aircraft to lose control and enter a steep dive from which recovery was not possible prior to terrain impact.

factors.evidence: While flying in the vicinity of Quebec City at an altitude of approx. 6,000 feet, Flight 315 flew into a cumulonimbus cloud
Encountering severe turbulence, the aircraft somehow lost control and went into a near-vertical dive from which it could not recover
the aircraft slammed into the ground near Issoudun in a 70-degree nose-down position

events.text: Aircraft flying at 6,000 feet near Quebec City flew into a cumulonimbus cloud
Severe turbulence encountered after entering cloud
Aircraft lost control and went into a near-vertical dive
Aircraft slammed into the ground near Issoudun at speed over 200 knots in 70-degree nose-down position
